name: San Juan
tagline: Caribbean Living with US Citizenship Benefits
description: San Juan offers the rare combination of tropical Caribbean living under the American flag. No passport needed, no currency exchange, and access to US banking and healthcare systems, all wrapped in 500 years of Spanish colonial history. Act 60 tax incentives make it especially attractive for investors, though the cost of living is moderate by Caribbean standards. Old San Juan's colorful streets and the island's stunning beaches make it a genuinely special place to call home.

quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – tourist areas are safe; exercise caution elsewhere
quickFacts.climate: Tropical maritime with warm temperatures year-round

housing.description: Studio or older 1BR inland in Santurce, Río Piedras, or Hato Rey — walkable-ish, not beachfront

dining.description: Local fondas, Piñones food kiosks, and La Placita de Santurce a few times a week; mostly cooking at home

healthcare.description: Individual commercial plan bought directly from a Puerto Rico insurer (e.g., Triple-S Directo Bronze or First Medical); there is no ACA marketplace or subsidy in Puerto Rico, and the network is PR-only (emergency-only on the mainland). Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more

transportation.description: An older paid-off car on minimum PR insurance, or AMA buses plus Uber in the walkable core

entertainment.description: Beach days, Old San Juan walks, free festivals, and La Placita nightlife

1M.lifestyle: A studio or older 1BR inland in Santurce, Río Piedras, or Hato Rey keeps housing within reach, trading a beachfront address for a walkable, safer pocket. Groceries carry the Jones Act shipping premium — noticeably above the mainland — and LUMA electricity is both expensive and unreliable, so the utilities line stays stubborn. Health cover is an individual commercial plan bought straight from a Puerto Rico insurer, not a healthcare.gov ACA plan: there is no marketplace or subsidy on the island, and the network reaches the mainland only for emergencies. Days lean on the free stuff — beaches, Old San Juan, La Placita — with US-territory status meaning no passport, no visa, and US banking throughout.

2M.lifestyle: A furnished 1BR in Santurce, the Ocean Park edge, or Isla Verde adds amenities and a shorter walk to the sand. Dining out becomes a regular habit across Condado and Santurce, anchored by the island's weekend brunch culture, and a reliable car with full coverage opens up El Yunque, Rincón's surf, and the bioluminescent bays. Health cover moves to a better PR commercial plan with lower cost-sharing. Costs are moderate by Caribbean standards but above mainland Latin America — housing and the US-priced healthcare line take the biggest bites.

3M.lifestyle: A nice furnished 1BR in Condado or Old San Juan buys a premium, walkable address near the water. Dining at Marmalade, 1919, and Cocina Abierta becomes routine, a late-model SUV handles the island, and health cover steps up to a top local commercial PPO with a broad network. Deep-sea fishing, a premium gym, and the city's cultural calendar fill the rest. The US legal and banking framework provides a security most Caribbean destinations can't match — and at this level there is comfortable margin on top of it.

5M.lifestyle: An oceanview high-rise in Condado or a well-appointed Ocean Park address puts the beach and the restaurant scene at hand, with a weekly housekeeper keeping the home. Dining is near-daily at the island's best tables with the occasional private chef, and healthcare layers concierge or direct primary care and genuine mainland-US specialist access on top of a premium plan — because PR-only networks cover the mainland for emergencies only, that access is a real add-on cost. Yacht charters, golf, and Caribbean island-hopping define the leisure. For qualifying investors, Act 60 tax incentives can provide meaningful advantages at this level.

10M.lifestyle: A Condado oceanfront penthouse or a Dorado Beach estate rental anchors life at the top, kept by a part-time housekeeper and a grounds service — help here is priced at US mainland rates. Dining mixes the island's finest rooms with occasional private-chef evenings, transportation means multiple luxury vehicles, a boat, and charters, and healthcare pairs concierge medicine with a top-tier, mainland-priced plan for genuine US specialist access rather than a worldwide-expat policy — being US soil, San Juan reaches for the mainland, not an international network. A private yacht, Dorado Beach golf, sport fishing, and first-class global travel round it out. The US-territory framework — banking, legal system, and citizenship — is the differentiator no foreign Caribbean destination can match.
